analysis: The big gains came from the iou_delta reward with a 5.0 success bonus and a 0.01 step penalty, together with stronger optimisation (lr 0.001, 4 epochs). Together they took dev success from 0.33 to about 0.997. Heightmaps scored only 0.34, so the dev set does test overhangs and the voxel results are believable. Since then every recipe sits between 0.990 and 1.000. Seed-to-seed spread is about ±0.004, which is 1 to 3 failures out of 512 designs. Several recipes average about 0.997: t05/t09/t12, the four t14 seeds, and layernorm at lr 0.001 (t23–t25). t26 (layernorm, lr 0.0015) scored 1.0 with the highest train success, but on one seed only. The hidden test retrains the recipe, so the best use of the last round is replicates, not new single-seed variants that could win the max by luck.

proposals.hypothesis: Noise test: exact repeat of t26 (layernorm, lr 0.0015) with a new seed. If it scores 0.996 or higher, t26's 1.0 reflects a reliable recipe. A score below 0.994 means it was seed luck.

Noise test: second exact repeat of t26 with another seed. Its train success should stay at 0.988 or higher. If the t26 seeds average below 0.997, the recipe is no better than plain layernorm at lr 0.001 or t14.

Noise test: third exact repeat of t26, giving it four seeds to compare with t14's four. If the four t26 seeds average 0.998 or higher with a minimum of at least 0.996, t26 is the most reliable recipe. Otherwise prefer the recipe with the higher mean over its seeds.

Noise test: a fourth exact repeat of t23 (layernorm, lr 0.001), so it has as many seeds as t26 and t14 and the three can be compared fairly. If it scores 0.996 or higher, layernorm at lr 0.001 is as reliable as the alternatives. A lower score favours t26 or t14.
